items.note: The only documentary in the main competition, built on interviews with 24 Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers who operated the Gaza targeting systems, and named for the Hebrew military acronym for the number of civilians expected to be killed in a strike. Its premiere on 10 September drew a record standing ovation of about twenty-four and a half minutes.

items.event: Israel's culture minister announces that he will seek to revoke the citizenship of the filmmakers behind NAZA
items.note: Miki Zohar called the film vile and the award shocking and said he would act immediately to revoke the citizenship of the directors for betraying the state; Itamar Ben-Gvir told them to leave the country. The Culture Minister holds no such power: revocation runs under Article 11(b)(2) of the Citizenship Law, 5712-1952, through an application by the Interior Minister to a court for administrative affairs, on criteria the Supreme Court enumerated in Zayoud (21 July 2022) as terrorism, treason or serious espionage.

items.event: Israeli ministers move to strip the NAZA filmmakers of citizenship
items.note: A day after the documentary NAZA won the Special Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, Culture Minister Miki Zohar wrote that he would act “immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for betraying the state,” and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called the two directors a “disgrace and an embarrassment.” The Culture Minister holds no such power: revocation runs under Article 11(b)(2) of the Citizenship Law, 5712-1952 through a court for administrative affairs on the Interior Minister's application, and the criteria the Supreme Court set out in Zayoud (2022) are terrorism, treason or serious espionage. §14.1C.

items.event: UK Lawyers for Israel asks the Home Secretary to proscribe Médecins Sans Frontières under the Terrorism Act 2000
items.note: The letter to Shabana Mahmood rests on two named individuals, one claimed posthumously by Palestinian Islamic Jihad and one named on an Israeli allegation; proscription would make membership of or support for MSF an offence carrying up to fourteen years, on the precedent of Palestine Action in July 2025. MSF: "We would never knowingly employ people engaging in military activity."

items.event: Macklemore removed from Ed Sheeran's US tour after onstage “Free Palestine” statements
items.note: Messina Touring Group told Rolling Stone it had been notified by venues that they would not allow a concert with Macklemore on the lineup. Seven stadiums were reported as objecting, covering eight of the last ten US dates. Ed Sheeran made no public statement. At MetLife Stadium on 4 and 5 September Macklemore had told the crowd that criticism of Israel, of apartheid and of genocide is in no way a criticism of Jewish people. Macklemore published a statement the same day naming Sheeran and his team as having made the decision, quoting Sheeran's position as “I don’t take sides”, and arguing that there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed. The passages describing private conversations are his account and are unconfirmed by the other parties.

items.event: The Chief of the General Staff directs the Military Advocate General at the film and its sources
items.note: Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir instructed the Military Advocate General, Maj. Gen. Itai Ofir, to “examine and advance possible legal actions regarding the film and those involved in it,” and ordered an examination of “information security aspects and possible individuals involved in the leaking of classified materials” — an effort to identify the twenty-four anonymous serving and former personnel who testified. He called the film “blood libels” while stating in the same remarks that he had not watched it. The same day Netanyahu called the award “shocking” on Telegram and Zohar asked the authorities to consider whether the film's making amounted to “aiding the enemy during wartime,” an offence carrying life imprisonment or death under section 99 of the Penal Law, 5737-1977. §14.1D.

items.event: PACBI calls on Ed Sheeran to cancel his US tour and on opening artists to boycott it
items.note: The Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel asked him "to cancel his now compromised US tour" and, until then, called on "opening artists, audience members and, where possible, crew members to boycott the complicit tour." A 15 September addendum asked him to reinvite Macklemore.

items.event: Declassified UK names six further British charities fundraising for illegal settlements
items.note: Reporting by Melissa Müller identified six registered charities that appear to have sent more than £1.7 million to recipients in settlements over three years, four of them linked to Modiin Illit and the others to Alon Shvut and Ariel. Two state in their own filings that they support named settlements. None responded to the outlet; filed contact details for five did not work. The ICJP has complained to the Commission and the Metropolitan Police about one of them, and the Met said it had received 248 referrals relating to the war since October 2023 with no UK-based investigation under way. Recorded at §15.3A.

items.event: Ed Sheeran states that venues threatened to pull the shows and confirms Robert Kraft was one of them
items.note: Eleven days after the MetLife set, the headline act posts a statement to Instagram: the removal “was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine”, and of the venue owners who said they would pull the shows, Kraft was “one of those people”. Every tour date is kept.

items.event: Jury at Southwark Crown Court acquits the Churchill statue defendant of criminal damage
items.note: The second British jury within eight months to refuse to convict in a case arising from direct action over Gaza, after the Filton acquittals of 4 February 2026. The verdict is general, so it gives no reasons and creates no precedent.

items.event: More than 130 lawyers, former judges and legal academics tell Prime Minister Andy Burnham the settlement sanctions fall far short of UK obligations
items.note: The six-page letter demands sanctions on insurance, accountancy and digital infrastructure, a full arms embargo under Article 6(3) of the Arms Trade Treaty, and the breadth of measures applied to Russia.

items.event: Roger Waters posts a video captioned "Ed Who?"
items.note: On the night of 15 September 2026, hours after Ed Sheeran's statement on Macklemore's removal from the Loop Tour, Roger Waters posted a short video captioned "Ed Who?". He said there are "two kinds of people in this world", placed Macklemore among those who do "the right thing", and addressed Sheeran as one of the "pricks like you who do the wrong thing. Goodbye." The remark was reported the following day in the form "little prick" (§15.12).

items.event: A Fox News host asks what in the stage remarks was objectionable
items.note: On Fox News's panel programme The Five, host Jesse Watters questioned the stated ground for Macklemore's removal: "So what did he say that was bad?"; "He said 'Free Palestine?' Is that all?"; and "OK, well, all I heard was 'Free Palestine,'" adding, "I don't think that's hate speech." He nonetheless endorsed the outcome on proprietary grounds: "If Bob Kraft doesn't want you there ... you're gone! Who cares?" His co-host Greg Gutfeld called Macklemore "scum" for describing Israel's conduct as genocide. Recorded because a hostile witness on the programme that defended the removal could not identify anything in the remarks matching the description under which they were removed (§15.12).

items.event: Two members of Congress address the Loop Tour removal
items.note: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez tells TMZ the matter is “not just about one music artist or two music artists” but about what Robert Kraft did “to line up all of the stadiums, to censor speech in that one specific way,” and that “we need to be very clear about how dangerous a precedent this is”; she notes the mechanism is not subject-specific (“It could be speaking out about AI”). Representative Rashida Tlaib, the only Palestinian-American member of Congress, says of the headline act’s refusal to back the removed performer that “it just shows who’s courageous and who’s not,” and that platforms are used for human rights “but it seems there’s always an exception when it comes to Palestinian lives.” The report declines to adopt Tlaib’s First Amendment characterisation, since the owner of a privately held stadium is not a state actor.

items.event: Every remaining support act withdraws from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour
items.note: Aaron Rowe, Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas announced withdrawals on the same day. Rowe and Lukas Graham had been booked to fill the slots the removal of Macklemore created. Finneas: "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed." Lukas Graham: "Money doesn't give you the right to own the conversation."

items.event: Artists across the industry publicly back Macklemore after the Loop Tour removal
items.note: Kneecap ("Free Palestine. They can never silence the truth"), Bob Vylan ("There is no thanks for a duty"), Garbage ("Those who exile, silence and censor others are never the good guys"), Kehlani, CMAT, Ms. Rachel, MUNA, Paloma Faith, Greta Thunberg, Zara Larsson and PinkPantheress. Kneecap and Bob Vylan were both subjects of the June 2025 Avon and Somerset Police investigation into their Glastonbury sets. (Irish News; Billboard; BuzzFeed UK.)

items.event: Paloma Faith says quitting the tour would be right, and calls the question nuanced
items.note: Channel 4 News published an episode of its podcast The Fourcast titled "Paloma Faith: Ed Sheeran should QUIT TOUR over Palestine row". Asked whether Ed Sheeran should leave the remaining dates of the Loop Tour after Macklemore's removal, Paloma Faith said the question was "more nuanced than that" while stating that "ideologically it would be the right thing to do". She had already commented beneath Macklemore's own statement, calling him "a rare and important voice" and "a hero" (§15.12).

items.event: The petitioning organisation states on the BBC what it takes the words to mean
items.note: Elan Carr, chief executive of the Israeli-American Council, which circulated the 6-8 September petition seeking Macklemore's removal from the Loop Tour, was interviewed on BBC Radio 4's Today programme. He called the stage remarks "outrageous", said the performer had taken a "captive audience of tens of thousands" and gone on to "slander the State of Israel and the Jewish people", and said "he put forth a blood libel against the state of Israel, and by connection, the Jewish people". Of the slogan itself: "Free Palestine absolutely is a call for the extermination of the State of Israel and the Jewish People." He added that the performer "has no right to hijack a stage at a concert", that political statements have "no place in a concert", which "is supposed to be inclusive", and that the removal was "entirely appropriate". Carr was United States Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Anti-Semitism from 2019 to 2021 and told the Conference of Presidents of Major American Jewish Organizations in Jerusalem in February 2019: "I will work to eradicate the attempted distinction between anti-Zionism and anti-Semitism. There is no distinction." The stage remarks to which the characterisation was applied made the opposite distinction expressly: "Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you."

items.event: Massive Attack answer the "professional platform" reasoning point by point
items.note: Massive Attack posted a statement to Instagram responding to Ed Sheeran's statement of 15 September 2026: "Entertainment can never be bigger than resisting the apartheid & genocide of fellow human beings"; "'Neutrality' in the face of the slaughter of more than 20,000 children can never be neutrality"; and "no artist should tolerate the censorship of another artist, however many millions of dollars are in play". They described an "arc of state, corporate and media silence that allowed a genocide to take place" as seeking to coerce high-profile artists and actors into that silence, and closed: "We stand in solidarity with all artists risking their careers in defence of the rights of the Palestinian people" (§15.12).

items.event: Garbage issue a second statement addressed to Ed Sheeran by name
items.note: Having called the removal "madness. Sheer madness" on 15 September, Garbage posted again on 16 September 2026, calling the response "a major turning point" and writing that "the global consciousness has shifted" and that normalising or sanitising an apartheid state "will no longer be tolerated". Addressing the headline act directly: "Ed, there is only one victim here: the Palestinian people." The band commended Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe, and ticket-holders seeking refunds, as "choosing to stand with their conscience" (§15.12).

items.event: Two former support acts state a position without withdrawing, because their dates had ended
items.note: Myles Smith, BRIT Rising Star 2025, answered calls to leave a tour he had already finished: "For everyone asking me to drop out of Ed's tour, let's get something straight: I'm not on that tour anymore." He declined to turn on Sheeran, whom he called a friend who had "put more time, care and money into making the world better than most people will ever know", and added: "My solidarity will never be selective." The Irish band BIIRD, whose final tour date was the MetLife Stadium show at which the remarks were made, posted: "We stand unequivocally behind every word he said," placing their support with the people of Palestine, with the artists who stepped away, and with "anybody that speaks up against Zionist lobbying groups". The Irish group Amble, who played Phoenix and Nashville in June, said they could not withdraw from a tour they were no longer on. None of the three withdrew, and none is counted among the four withdrawals of 15 September (§15.12).

items.event: Reported audience figures across the removal week, with their limits
items.note: Newsweek, drawing on Social Blade, reported that Ed Sheeran's Instagram following fell by 43,648 on 14 September, by 149,635 on 15 September and by a further 70,111 by the morning of 16 September, a total of 263,394 across roughly two and a half days, against a fourteen-day net figure of 219,000. Macklemore gained 750,098 followers in the twenty-four hours after announcing the removal, passing 7.9 million; Sheeran's count fell to 47.3 million; Aaron Rowe grew his following by 73 per cent to more than 132,000; and the five acts together gained approximately 1.6 million, more than seven times the reported loss. Limits: these are net third-party estimates rather than an audited platform record, the 16 September figure was incomplete when reported, and at least one outlet noted that no independent public record confirms the precise change (§15.12).

items.event: Tommy Robinson posts in support of Ed Sheeran
items.note: The British far-right activist Tommy Robinson (Stephen Yaxley-Lennon) posted on X in support of Ed Sheeran over Macklemore's removal, tagging him directly, adding an expletive remark against Palestinians and dismissing critics as "middle class brats who live in suburbia". Carried by a single outlet quoting it directly and recorded as reported there rather than as independently corroborated; no response from Sheeran or his representatives is documented (§15.12).

items.event: Lewis Hamilton and the scale of the endorsement
items.note: Forbes reports that Macklemore’s statement of 14 September has passed 7.2 million likes, and that the seven-time Formula One world champion Sir Lewis Hamilton commented on it: “Thank you for using your voice, standing with you.” Kehlani’s comment alone draws close to 400,000 likes. Forbes names Florence Pugh, Penelope Cruz, Rachel Zegler, Cara Delevingne, Amanda Seyfried, Chase Infiniti, Bella Hadid and Hozier as endorsing the post without commenting. A like is not a position and is not recorded as one.

items.event: A governing-party legislator states that international law does not apply to Israel
items.note: Likud MK Hanoch Milwidsky, speaking on the mission and religious identity of the Jewish people and reported by Israel's Channel 13: “We are not like everyone else, and therefore all the laws that apply to everyone cannot apply to us,” adding that “the considerations of all kinds of statesmen from around the world should not be relevant to us.” The same legislator told the Knesset on 29 July 2024, of a detainee raped at Sde Teiman, “if he is a Nukhba, everything is legitimate to do.” Article 27 of the Vienna Convention forecloses even the stronger claim that internal law excuses non-performance of a treaty.

items.event: Four NFL stadium owners named in the Loop Tour removal
items.note: The Wall Street Journal reported that representatives of Robert Kraft (New England Patriots), David Tepper (Carolina Panthers), Arthur Blank (Atlanta Falcons) and Jeffrey Lurie (Philadelphia Eagles) contacted Messina Touring Group after the MetLife Stadium show of 4 September 2026, and that the owners were told the issue of Palestine would not be raised again from the stage. Macklemore raised it again on 5 September. Three of the owners threatened to cancel their dates. Kraft and Ed Sheeran then spoke for forty minutes, Kraft expressing sympathy for Palestinians while describing the remarks as hate speech. Macklemore had been booked for ten dates and was removed from the remaining eight. The reporting corroborates the collective element of Macklemore's own account; it does not identify who gave the assurance or with what authority.

items.event: A Palestinian flag is raised from a stage in Orlando without consequence
items.note: Gorillaz open their North American tour at the Kia Center in Orlando. Damon Albarn takes a Palestinian flag from the audience, holds it above his head and tells the crowd: "Don't forget this. Ever. Stand your position. Don't ever be neutral." Thirteen days after the MetLife Stadium remarks that led to Macklemore's removal, and in the same country, no venue cancels and no act is dropped. The Orlando arena is owned by the City of Orlando, not by a private proprietor.

items.event: The Intercept publishes the Kraft Family Foundation filings
items.note: Jonah Valdez, analysing Kraft Family Foundation tax filings back to 2006 and Kraft Group FEC disclosures, recorded $196,000 to Friends of the IDF across seven gifts each earmarked "Promote education for young Jewish soldiers", $123,000 between Brothers for Life and Friends of Israel Disabled Veterans, $150,000 to MEMRI, $63,500 to CAMERA and $50,000 to the Investigative Project on Terrorism. The removal statement had offered the donor's philanthropy, including resources "directed to Palestine", as part of its ground. No donation in the filings names a Palestinian recipient. The giving is lawful and publicly filed; it is recorded because the statement itself made it checkable.

items.event: The donation and the matches
items.note: Macklemore gave $1 million, the whole of his net Loop Tour earnings, to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund, HEAL Palestine, the Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Anera and UNRWA, citing "everything that has happened over the last 48 hours". Robert Kraft matched it with $2 million, stating that Ed Sheeran had asked him for the match and that Sheeran planned to approach other venue owners to "build bridges". Rachel Accurso (Ms. Rachel) matched $1 million to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund on 18 September, writing: "I will match Macklemore's donation and I invite every wealthy white celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza." Mara Kronenfeld of UNRWA USA recorded more than $509,000 already directed to the agency by "Hind's Hall" and its sequel.

items.event: Six Palestinians killed in Gaza in one day, among them a ten-year-old girl and the health ministry director-general's son
items.note: Israeli fire killed six across the Strip on 19 September 2026, eleven months into the ceasefire: Basir al-Bursh, eldest son of Gaza Ministry of Health director-general Dr Munir al-Bursh, struck by a drone missile as he stepped out of a tent in az-Zahra west of Jabalia and pronounced dead on arrival; a ten-year-old girl who died at al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital of wounds from Israeli gunfire north of Nuseirat; one killed and at least four wounded, two of them children, by a drone strike on a vehicle in the Sheikh Radwan market; one killed in Shujayea. The Israeli military said it had struck 'several militants' including Basir al-Bursh, without giving further information. Ministry of Health figures that day: 1,386 killed and 4,784 wounded since the ceasefire of 10 October 2025.
